scandal_summary: Tesco overstated commercial income (supplier rebates) by £263 million in H1 2014, recognised as income based on forecast customer behaviour rather than actuals. PwC had signed off FY2013/14 with only 19 supplier confirmations (12 returned) out of >2,000 suppliers, covering ~8% of commercial income by value. The FRC later found PwC failed to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence and failed to consider fraud risk in commercial income. 30+ years of PwC tenure at Tesco.
key_red_flags_that_should_have_been_rais: Commercial income £202M in H1 — rebate accrual methodology relied on forecast customer behaviour, not actuals; this is an aggressive recognition policy that departs from prior-year practice
Sample of 19 suppliers out of >2,000 — only 8% of commercial income by value independently confirmed
Only 12 of 19 supplier confirmations returned (63% response rate) — low confirmation rate on a high-risk account
Reliance on management representations for a known fraud-risk area — supplier rebates are routinely cited in retail fraud literature
30+ year PwC tenure at Tesco — long tenure associated with reduced skepticism
Commercial income line grew faster than revenue — divergence between income and revenue growth is a classic falsification signal
No substantive analytical procedures on the rebate accrual methodology change in 2013/14 — methodology changes warrant heightened attention, not trend-based testing
Lack of fraud brainstorming (ISA 240) specifically on commercial income — high-risk by category, requires explicit consideration

expected_judgement_axes.evidence_sufficiency: Insufficient — sample of 19 suppliers, 63% confirmation rate, 8% coverage; this fails ISA 530 sampling adequacy for a high-risk account.
expected_judgement_axes.going_concern: Not the main issue; the issue is the audit-evidence quality on commercial income.
